newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - C&W seen set to leave German alliance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - C&W seen set to leave German alliance.

text.p: Fears of too little management control and too much costly investment in infrastructure spurred Cable and Wireless Plc to reconsider plans to forge an alliance with two German utilities, industry sources said on Tuesday.

Analysts said the British telecoms firm seemed certain to walk away from the partnership and the only questions remaining were the terms of its departure and the plans it has up its sleeve once it goes.
"The partnership has clearly broken up," Salomon Brothers analyst Andrew Harrington said. "We're just waiting to see the details of their departure."

C&W and Veba formed a strategic alliance, called Vebacom, in 1995. Last year, the firms agreed to bring RWE into the alliance and final contracts were drawn up two weeks ago. But C&W has not signed and evidence is growing that it may pull out.

Industry sources said C&W faced a divergence of strategy with its German partners. Veba and RWE favoured heavy investment in infrastructure in Germany but C&W was wary of having to commit too many resources to Vebacom, they said.

Too big a commitment to Vebacom would hamper plans to expand cable company C&W Communications in Europe. Industry sources said C&W intended to make development of this company a major plank of its European strategy.

Industry sources said a shift in the balance of power in the alliance if RWE came on board was also a concern. C&W was said to be worried it would have too little influence in the management of the enlarged partnership.

Analysts said the investment required by the German project was certainly a factor in C&W's likely departure. "C&W is not a big enough company to provide all the funding that was necessary in order to establish Vebacom as a meaningful telecom asset in Germany," Harrington said.
But they said C&W was also likely to have an alternative plan up its sleeve, which required leaving the partnership.

Most said it looked set to join forces with a major global telecoms alliance. Global One, partnership of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp of the U.S., is widely regarded as the most likely candidate.

"I think they are going to be part of a global carrier at some point in the next year, and that will crystallise the very high strategic value of C&W's asset base," Harrington said. "Global One is the most likely option -- either through a joint venture but more probably a stake," he said.
A deal with C&W would be a good coup for Global One as it would give it access to lucrative Asian and British markets.
"C&W has a unique asset base that would fit in very well with any other global carrier," Harrington said. "But they are not big enough to be a global carrier by themselves."

But pulling out of the German alliance could be pose problems -- C&W must find a buyer for its 45-percent stake in Vebacom, and risks short-term share instability if Veba sells its 10.5-percent C&W stake.

A senior Veba source said on Tuesday that the firm had offered to buy back C&W's 45-percent stake in Vebacom and hold it in the hope of selling it to a new partner. Veba would retain its stake in C&W, the source said.
Analysts said the offer seemed reasonable and discussions were probably now centering on how much C&W would get for its Vebacom stake.
He said even if Veba was disinclined to buy back C&W's Vebacom stake, another buyer could be found. Analysts said SBC Communications and BellSouth Corp were both potential buyers.
